description:
The backlog accumulated faster than it was maintained. At the point this epic was
opened there were 79 open/in-progress tickets, 64 of them filed in June/July
2026, and most described a world that no longer exists: symptoms fixed by
unrelated work, repros that no longer reproduce, named tests that have been
deleted, and measurements taken against inputs since shrunk by 5x.

That is worse than a big backlog. A ticket whose description is stale sends the
next person to the wrong file, and one whose repro passes wastes a whole session
before anyone doubts the ticket instead of the code.

## What this epic is

The re-baselined backlog. Every child here has been RE-VERIFIED against main
417c5b0b5 -- the merge point of the fz-go4.1..fz-f98.24 stack, where the suite is
fully green (lib 1454/0, matrix 416/0, fz2_cli 20/0, aot_variadic_open 1/0,
doc-tests 210/0, on CI as well as locally).

## The rule

- A ticket whose defect no longer reproduces is CLOSED, with the evidence and an
  explicit note that it closed on absence of a repro rather than an attributed
  fix, plus instructions to file fresh rather than reopen.
- A ticket that is STILL VALID is rewritten as a new child of this epic, stating
  only what is true now, and the original is closed pointing at the successor.
- No contradictory comment layers. If the description is wrong, the description
  changes. A ticket is persistent memory; it should read as current state, not
  as an archaeological record.

## What a child must carry

- A repro that was RUN, with its actual output, not a remembered one.
- Where the old ticket was wrong, said plainly, so nobody re-derives the dead
  diagnosis.
- Checks that are decidable.
- Elixir's answer where the subject is language behaviour.
title: Re-baseline the compiler backlog against main 417c5b0b5
